  \caption{Cost of proving $N = 2^{n}$ integer multiplications $x \cdot y = z$, $n = 15, \ldots, 22$, for random $32$-bit integers $x, y$ (so that $z$ is a $64$-bit integer) with \cref{c:iop_pimsat}: one R1CS constraint per multiplication over $\ZZ$, projected to a prime $q$ sampled after the commitment from an interval $[2^{b-1}, 2^{b})$ with $b$ between $108$ and $111$ depending on the shape, a Spartan PIOP over $\FF_q$ (with a $3$-variable univariate skip), bitification, and the \ftwoz\ opening of the $128$ bits committed per multiplication ($\codedim = 2^{n+7}$ bits in cells of $W = 1$ bit, i.e.\ $128$ cells per multiplication). Security profile $\lambda = 100$: every round-by-round error is at most $2^{-100.0}$, the binding term being \texttt{step5\_3:ligerito-tracked}; the commitment is opened with ring switching and Ligerito~\cite{ligerito} over a Reed--Solomon code of rate $1/8$ over $\FF_{2^{128}}$ (initial folding of $2^{4}$ rows, Johnson regime, BLAKE3 Merkle trees), configured for $100$ bits — the same opener as \cref{tab:f2z-raw-performance}. \emph{Witness} is the witness generation (the products $z = x \cdot y$ and the Spartan assignment) from the operand pairs; it is not part of the prover time. Prover columns: \emph{Commit} is bit packing plus the commitment; \emph{PIOP} is the prime projection, the Spartan PIOP and the (microsecond-scale) bitification step; \emph{grand products}, \emph{ring switch} and \emph{Ligerito} are the three parts of the \ftwoz\ opening as in \cref{tab:f2z-raw-performance}; \emph{Total} is end to end and includes the commitment (each entry is a median, so the parts need not add up exactly). Proof columns: \emph{PIOP} is the Spartan messages and grinding nonces; \emph{Non-Lig.} is the opening's integer folds, GKR, sumcheck and ring-switch messages; \emph{Ligerito} is the Ligerito proof; KB $= 1000$ bytes.
